correctness.rationale: Exact Cauchy support identity reduces perimeter to the expectation of a capped triangular linear projection in southwest directions. A triangular area ratio gives survival (1-t^2/(ab))^n. Swapping two nonnegative integrals yields an exact one-variable kernel. The beta integral produces each rational inverse-factorial term and signed Taylor remainders establish strict alternating error bounds and absolute convergence for every n>=0. Gamma-ratio asymptotics prove the claimed n^(-1/2), n^(-3/2), and n^(-2) terms; independent one-point/zero-point calculations and a standalone quadrature/simulation checker corroborate the proof without replacing it.

value.rationale: The natural Euclidean mean length of a random convex chain is mathematically distinct from its area moments and vertex-count laws in current same mathematical model literature. The result gives an exact evaluated expectation for every sample size, explicit convergent strict upper/lower bounds at arbitrary order, and a geometrically interpretable slower n^(-1/2) boundary deficit with a separate n^(-2) corner term. This exact self-contained observable provides rigorous benchmarks for random-polytope boundary approximation; the right-triangle model is canonical, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
